name: [[512,18,19]] weight-8 planar tile code on a 16x16 lattice

provenance.construction: Open-boundary weight-8 planar tile code (bivariate bicycle) on a 16x16 lattice via research/local2d/boundary_engine.build_planar: A-support f={(0,0),(0,3),(2,2),(3,0)}, B-support g={(0,2),(1,3),(2,0),(3,3)} (two supports, second-order boundary generators completed by exact half-infinite boundary gauge operators over F2[t] with corner topological-order completion). The same call at (21,22) reproduces the board's codes/924-18-31.json check-for-check, which calibrates the generator; 16x16 is the same construction at the smaller lattice size at which arXiv:2504.09171 reports d=19. Layout is the square-grid coordinate map planar.grid_coordinates(16,16) with 2 qubits per site, layers=2.
provenance.notes: Independent reconstruction, not a new construction. The parameters are those of the weight-8 planar tile-code family of arXiv:2504.09171 at a 16x16 lattice; the same generator call at (21,22) reproduces the board's codes/924-18-31.json check-for-check, so the family is calibrated rather than inferred. arXiv:2504.09171 reports [[512,18,19]] with d=19 stated exact, and the witness search run here did NOT reproduce that reading: it found a weight-18 Z-side logical, so this entry claims d<=18, not d<=19. That is an upper bound from an explicit witness, not an exact claim; exact certification is the maintainer-side verify/certify.py tier and is not asserted here. A sibling B-support, g={(0,1),(1,1),(2,0),(3,3)}, which the board's codes/566-18-20 records for this family, also yields n=512, k=18, w=8 on a 16x16 lattice, so two distinct codes carry these parameters; this entry's check matrices fix which one it is, and no claim is made about the other. On the Pareto frontier this entry is additive rather than displacing: nothing on the board is dominated by it, and it does not lead its cell on kd^2/n (11.39 against [[155,6,23]] at 20.48). It adds a new nondominated point at n=512, k=18, which is below every existing k=18 tile entry (n=562, n=563, n=924).
